[b]Opening of Nuclear Facilities, 12th Feb, 2028[/b]

The Federal Republic of Valddera today formally announces the launch of a comprehensive national nuclear energy initiative, marking a decisive step toward long-term energy security and technological advancement. Framed as a cornerstone of national reliance on external energy sources while supporting the rapid growth of Valddera's industrial and urban sectors. At the center of the initiative lies the launch of multiple civilian nuclear power facilities across the western and coastal regions, designed to provide stable, high-capacity energy to both population centers and emerging economic zones. Government officials emphasized that the program is set to adhere to international safety standards and will be developed with focus on sustainability, efficiency, and domestic expertise. In notable detail, the Ministry of Energy confirmed that elements of Valddera's historic nuclear infrastructure will be repurposed and modernized to support the new program. Facilities once decommissioned in the 20th century have undergone established refurbishment, allowing the nation to draw upon its previously established technical  foundations. Archival research, scientific documentation, and legacy engineering designs are also being re-evaluated as part of the initiative. The government further outlined plans to establish a fully integrated nuclear fuel cycle within Valddera, ensuring that the nation maintains full control over fuel production, processing, and long-erm resource management. Officials described this as essential for guaranteeing uninterrupted energy supply and reinforcing national resilience in an increasingly uncertain global environment. While the announcement was framed firmly within context of civilian energy development, analysts have noted the strategic implicaitions of such a program, particularly given Valddera's historical advancement of nuclear technologies. In response, state representatives reiterated that the initiative is rooted in peaceful application, while also affirming the nation's right o pursue technological self-sufficiency.

[spoiler=Who are the potential candidates for the upcoming Wellassonan General Election?] 
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Sunday, 13 February 2028[/i]

Speculation has already kicked in as the next Wellassonan General Election, in which the Prime Minister is indirectly elected, are just over 5 months away.

The upcoming elections will be the 9th general elections since the end of communist rule in 1996. In the general election, voters vote for a political party, after which the winning party selects one of their party members to serve as prime minister until the next election. The Wellassonan election process is notorious for  being among the most confusing systems in the world, due to the fact that the PM, the head of government, is elected in a very similar manner to a head of state in other countries. The indirectness of the elections have also come into scrutiny in recent years. While the system is intended to entice voters to vote for party instead of individual, many criticise it as being undemocratic and that it gives the parties too much power.

Due to the tense atmosphere surrounding these elections, they are expected to be among the most heated elections since the transition to democracy. Coming into these elections, the leading political parties are the Socialists and the Toward the Future Party, with the other parties also looking to secure good results.

The Socialists, the current ruling party of the past 16 years, have been the most successful party in Wellassona since the return to democracy. Under the Premiership of Socialist Makar Krupinev from 2012 to 2020, Wellassona experienced massive economic growth, the fastest since the communist era. This means that it wasn't a surprise when the Socialists won the 2020 election as well. Danil Sokolova, an influential senator representing Rheyara, was chosen to be the PM. He was selected again to be the PM after the Socialist victory in 2024 as well. 

However, in his second term, Sokolova has quickly grown to be extremely unpopular, mainly due to his economic policies that have been seen as heavily draconic, even to many in the Socialist Party. His unpopularity has been a major reason for Socialist struggles in local elections, most notably in 2025, when the Socialists lost the Premiership in Rheyara to the Toward the Future Party. The Wellassonan Constitution forbids a person from being selected as Prime Minister for more than 2 consecutive terms, so Sokolova is ineligible to be selected if the Socialist were to win.

There are a few people that have been floated around as being possible Socialist choices for prime minister. Among the most likely is Kaldangan Kemurtevič. Kemurtevič, a Diet member representing Kemder, was the Socialist choice for Premier in that state's election the year prior. He however lost that election in a surprise upset for the far-right Reform the State party, whose Karina Lagounov emerged victorious. Despite this, being the leader of the Socialists in the Diet, he has an immense influence in the party. He is considered a moderate socialist, in contrast to Sokolova, who has been deemed a "radical" socialist during his second term. He is also rather young, at just 46, much younger than Sokolova, who is 79. All of these factors make Kemurtevič the most likely Socialist choice for PM according to political pundits. If elected, he would be the first person under 40, the first person from Kemder, and the first Muslim to be Prime Minister. Other Socialists that have been considered possibilities for PM include Apollinariya Yemistenhiya, the 1st Junior Minister, Stanislava Poyanmovov, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Onufriy Pavlovsky, a popular senator from Lomeckyj.

On the other hand, The main opposition, the Libertarian Toward the Future Party, has one clear choice for PM: Ipatiy Sergeev. A Senator representing Rheyara, Sergeev has been an influential voice in Wellassonan politics as of the past 6 years. An advocate of more laissez-faire economics and social conservatism, he has quickly been gaining popularity among those unhappy with the Sokolova administration. As the Toward the Future Party narrowly lead the polls, he is considered, at the moment, the most likely person to become PM.

Among the other parties, the Reform the State will likely choose the party head, Fergecko Senator Valya Kulikov. A staunch supporter of immigration control, she has proclaimed that Wellassona must cut immigration numbers, especially from Muslim countries. While supporters of her see her as a woman of the people trying to protect her nation's interests, many people criticise her for being Islamophobic, engaging in fearmongering, and promoting authoritarian policies. Her party currently rank third in the polls.

In the People's Party, the liberal party of the country, current Fergecko Premier Alik Irentik has expressed his intent to step down as Premier if his party is elected. He has been among the sharpest critics of Sokolova, particularly of his action of shifting the election schedule, which caused Irentik to not be able to run for a second term. He is considered unlikely to become PM.

Among the centrist Unity Party, the likely choice is inkenan Diet member Fyodor Lebedevi. Though a well supported politician among many, it is highly unlikely that his party is voted in this election. In contrast, for the Conservative party, there is a battle for the top spot between the 2 Conservative Torkamy Diet members, Matrona Andreeva and Pavel Felavkan. None are considered likely to become PM due to the relative unpopularity of the Conservatives outside Torkamy.

The Election for President will also take place concurrently with the election for PM. The President, who is the head of state in Wellassona, is a largely powerless position. Apart from the ability to introduce legislation and that of calling a no-confidence vote on the PM, the President is almost fully ceremonial. The current President, Socialist Vladimir Ubikicov, is unable to run for a 3rd term.The primaries took place 3 weeks ago, in which the following candidates were chosen: Akulino ukovka of the Socialists, Rurik Stephanovi of Toward the Future, and Yalek Kemevy of the People's Party. Only the top 3 parties in the diet at the time of the election can field candidates in the Presidential election.

Both the General and the Presidential Elections will take place on election day, 29 July, with the PM being chosen by the winning party in late August to early September, with them taking office on October 5.
